title: Worked examples: a peak lump sum, and waiting in cash
objectives: Compare peak vs perfect timing over 10 years, and day-one vs waiting a year.
Say why waiting has a cost too.
body_md:
Example 2: a lump sum at a peak. ₹10 lakh is invested just before a 40% fall. The market takes two years to recover to the starting level, then grows at an assumed 12% a year. Invested at the “perfect” time (no fall, 12% a year throughout): about ₹31.1 lakh after 10 years. Invested at the peak, then the fall and 2-year recovery: about ₹24.8 lakh after 10 years.

|  | Value after 10 years |
| --- | --- |
| Invested at the "perfect" time (no fall, 12% a year throughout) | ≈ ₹31.1 lakh |
| Invested at the peak, then the fall and 2-year recovery | ≈ ₹24.8 lakh |

The peak hurts, but with a long horizon the investment still grows substantially. Selling during the fall would have locked in the loss. Example 3: waiting in cash for “the right time”. An investor keeps ₹10 lakh in a deposit earning an assumed 6% for one year, waiting for a dip that doesn't come, then invests at an assumed 12% for nine years. Invested on day one: about ₹31.1 lakh after 10 years. Waited one year in cash: about ₹29.4 lakh after 10 years.

|  | Value after 10 years |
| --- | --- |
| Invested on day one | ≈ ₹31.1 lakh |
| Waited one year in cash | ≈ ₹29.4 lakh |

Waiting has a cost too. It feels safer, but it isn't free, and the dip it waits for may arrive only after the market has risen further.
example: Peak vs perfect over 10 years: about ₹24.8 lakh vs ₹31.1 lakh — the peak cost about ₹6.3 lakh, but the investment still more than doubled; selling in the fall would have locked in the loss.
say: The peak hurts, but a long horizon still grows the money.
Waiting feels safer, but it isn't free.
never: Investing at a peak means losing money over long horizons.

check.q: In the illustration, waiting a year in cash for a dip ended at ≈₹29.4 L versus ≈₹31.1 L invested on day one. The lesson is…
check.why: Waiting has a cost too. Missing time in the market can cost more than investing on a bad day.

check.q: In Example 2, the peak investment after 10 years was about:
o: ₹24.8 lakh, vs about ₹31.1 lakh for perfect timing
check.why: Invested at the peak, then the fall and 2-year recovery: about ₹24.8 lakh after 10 years.

check.q: In Example 3, waiting one year in cash cost about:
o: ₹1.7 lakh (₹31.1 lakh vs ₹29.4 lakh) over 10 years
check.why: Invested on day one: about ₹31.1 lakh. Waited one year in cash: about ₹29.4 lakh.
